clue.text: Be economical if you want extra money

definitions.meaning: to be thrifty is to hold back, or spare, your cash rather than spend it
funds left over after needs are met, available to splash out

explanation.surface: Advice that thrift is the way to build up a little surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a verb phrase it means save your money; read as a noun it is surplus funds, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Look which makes Peter lose heart

indicators.note: a word that loses its heart drops its central letter, here the middle of the name

explanation.surface: A question of which glance makes a man called Peter despondent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose heart' removes the middle letter T from PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look closely or with effort.

clue.text: Dealer's'clique allowed to acquire a decorative hair-piece

parts.note: a ring is a group of dealers who collude, for instance at auctions
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A dealers' cartel is permitted to buy an ornamental wig.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'ring' is a cartel of dealers who agree not to bid against each other at auction. The stray apostrophe in 'Dealer's'clique' comes from the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair, an ornamental part of a hairstyle.

clue.text: Unable to rest in peace because of a witch's spell

parts.note: can't means unable
RIP is the abbreviation for rest in peace, carved on gravestones

explanation.surface: Someone cannot lie quietly in the grave because a witch has cursed them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantrip is a Scots word for a magic charm or incantation.

clue.text: He looks and looks ahead

parts.note: one who sees is literally a see-er, and a prophet looks into the future

explanation.surface: A man who watches and also gazes forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet or visionary is someone who sees, including seeing what is to come.

clue.text: The team mates I settled together

indicators.note: settled suggests things being put in order, so these letters are rearranged into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The team-mates and I sorted ourselves out as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled' asks you to rearrange the letters of THE TEAM MATES I.
explanation.definitionFit: Simultaneously means happening as one, in unison.

clue.text: Normal lines of transmission for BBC1 and ITV?

definitions.text: Normal lines of transmission for BBC1 and ITV?

parts.words: Normal lines of transmission for BBC1 and ITV?
parts.note: the customary routes of communication, read literally as the familiar television stations of British broadcasting

explanation.surface: A question about how mainstream TV gets to viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: BBC1 and ITV are the long-established main British television stations, so they are the everyday channels in a literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the proper or customary official routes for communication.

clue.text: Ten Eton nurses abused? Fiddlesticks!

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or misused, so these letters are knocked into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An outraged cry about ten school nurses at Eton being mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' asks you to rearrange the letters of TEN ETON NURSES. Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish.

clue.text: A sailing ship heading South needs a chart, but only a rough one

indicators.note: the compass letter is placed at the head of the vessel, coming in front of it

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel
a map is a chart

explanation.surface: A ship sailing south carries a navigational chart, if only a crude one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' puts S in front of KETCH. 'one' in the definition points back to 'chart', so the definition is a rough chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch map is a hand-drawn outline drawing of an area without precise detail.

clue.text: Difficult man has skill, yet lacks finer feelings

parts.note: hard means difficult
he is the pronoun for a man
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A tricky fellow is talented but insensitive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what someone with this quality does: a person with this has no finer feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a heart of stone means being callous and unfeeling towards others.

clue.text: German Chancellor may get black eye with it in the East

definitions.meaning: Helmut ... led West Germany and then reunified Germany from 1982 to 1998

definitions.text: may get black eye with it in the East
definitions.meaning: a dark powder used as eyeliner across the Middle East and Asia

explanation.surface: A German leader might end up with a black eye somewhere in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Helmut, Germany's chancellor, is also the word for an Eastern eye cosmetic of powdered antimony.

clue.text: Show obvious disapproval of a large cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the word next to it is mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Frowning at someone over an oversized mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' asks you to rearrange the letters of LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To glare is to stare angrily, a clear sign of displeasure.

clue.text: The baby's mother has a double degree

indicators.note: double means the degree is written twice in succession

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: An infant's mum turns out to hold two degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a childish word for mother, the kind a baby says.

clue.text: A lot of politicians do

definitions.meaning: a political organisation of like-minded members, such as Labour
a do is an informal word for a celebration or social gathering

explanation.surface: Many politicians are in the habit of doing so.
explanation.definitionFit: A political group is one sense; a celebration such as a birthday bash is the other.

clue.text: The drinks taken by superior people, but not the teetotaller

indicators.note: not says the abstainer is left out of the group of superior people

parts.note: your betters are people of higher standing
TT is short for teetotal, one who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: Upper-class folk enjoy their drinks, except for the one who abstains.
explanation.definitionFit: Pints of ale and lager are alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: It once encouraged Anglicans to hold a rehearsal

definitions.meaning: an old English law requiring public office-holders to take Church of England communion, favouring Anglicans
to try out a performance, to trial a piece of theatre

explanation.surface: An old rule that once pushed churchgoers to hold a practice run.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test Act of 1673 barred non-Anglicans from public office in England until its repeal in 1828.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical statute favoured members of the established Church; read literally, it is trialling a performance.

clue.text: Holey holy creed wholly revised

parts.note: pi is a slang abbreviation for pious, meaning holy

indicators.note: the word beside it is completely reworked, giving a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A play on holey, holy and wholly about a religious creed being rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wholly revised' rearranges CREED into ERCED. PI as a short form of pious is an old crossword convention. The three sound-alikes holey, holy and wholly are a trap, and only the first one is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pierced has had holes punched through it.

clue.text: Pet found in many of Birmingham's terraces

indicators.note: the answer is discovered lying within the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A domestic animal kept in many of Birmingham's terraced houses.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside birmingHAM'S TERraces. Birmingham is England's second city; terraces are rows of joined houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rodent commonly kept in a cage as a household animal.

clue.text: One rooted in the Liberal tradition

definitions.meaning: from Latin radix, root: something at the root
the ... were the reforming wing of the British Liberal Party

explanation.surface: Someone deeply grounded in liberal values.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Latin for root, and also names the reformist strand of nineteenth-century British Liberal politics.

clue.text: Refuse to make period costume before time

indicators.note: before places the clothing ahead of the time in the answer

parts.note: garb is clothing, especially of a distinctive or historical style
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Declining to make costumes for a historical drama ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb, to decline, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste and rubbish thrown away is household trash.

clue.text: Well done! Drink up, old chum

parts.note: good! is an exclamation of approval

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat

explanation.surface: Congratulations, finish your drink, my old friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAP to PAL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A close friend of long standing.

clue.text: A section of the Bible become opposed to

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'A section of the Bible become opposed to', has A + NT (section of the Bible) but no word giving the final I; 'become' supplies nothing, so a word such as 'I' seems lost from the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: A section of the Bible become opposed to

clue.text: That fool Amin upset Transport Officer

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda in the 1970s

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters for the officer are turned back to front

parts.note: TO is the abbreviation for Transport Officer

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at the Ugandan dictator for overturning a transport official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TO around to give OT. Amin's first name stands in for the letters IDI; using a famous person's first name like this is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Exceptional person, but deficient in writing and arithmetic?

definitions.meaning: someone unique or remarkable, one of a kind
of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic)

explanation.surface: Someone outstanding who nonetheless struggles with sums and spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic; drop writing and arithmetic and you have ONE R.
explanation.definitionFit: It is British slang for a unique, remarkable individual.

clue.text: Advanced in fast time

definitions.meaning: the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Moving forward during a period of quick progress.
explanation.definitionFit: It means loaned, as money advanced to a borrower, and is the forty-day period of abstinence before Easter.

clue.text: Note played very loudly caused ill-temper

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A note blasted out at full volume put someone in a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A huff or petty fit of annoyance.

clue.text: I am sensible, but you'd never notice

parts.note: I'm is short for I am
in its older sense, sensible means able to be sensed or perceived

explanation.surface: A person boasting of good sense, adding that it is not obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sensible' is used in its older meaning, detectable by the senses, not level-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so slight it cannot be detected by any sense.

clue.text: The genre of painting that is not yet dead

definitions.meaning: pictures of arranged objects such as fruit or flowers
read literally, existence continuing, still being alive

explanation.surface: A kind of art that has not died out.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the art genre depicting inanimate objects, and read literally means life going on.
